result.title: No Frames, Just Frequencies: Bandwidth-Efficient Deployment-Time Adaptation for Smart Glasses
result.summary: Deep neural networks deployed on smart glasses must adapt to changes in the distribution of incoming data while adhering to strict privacy and device constraints. We present No Frames, Just Frequencies, a bandwidth-efficient source-assisted adaptation framework that characterizes distribution shifts using compact frequency descriptors computed on-device. Rather than transmitting camera frames, the glasses compute and send frequency descriptors to a host device that contains a replica of the model. The host device maps the received frequency descriptor to a distribution shift operator that synthesizes out-of-distribution data and adapts a model replica using a pre-defined adaptation protocol. We evaluate the framework on mixtures of ImageNet-C corruptions using convolution-based (ConvNeXtV2-Femto), self-attention-based (DeiT-Tiny), and hybrid (TinyViT-5M) vision models, on person classification (Visual Wake Words), and on object detection (MS-COCO). Our results reveal that adaptation driven solely by the transmitted descriptors recovers $93-95\%$ of the supervised oracle adaptation gain on all three architectures, $82\%$ on Visual Wake Words and $94$--$98\%$ on MS-COCO. Notably, adaptation quality degrades gracefully as the descriptor resolution decreases from $224 $ to $28$ pixels, consistently across architectures, enabling bandwidth reductions from $213\times$ to $784\times$ across the frequency descriptors.

AI.brief_summary: 提出面向智能眼镜的带宽高效自适应框架：设备端计算紧凑频率描述子而非上传图像帧，主机端据此生成分布偏移算子、合成 OOD 数据并更新模型副本，在多种视觉模型及分类、检测任务上验证可恢复大部分 oracle 自适应收益，且描述子分辨率下降时性能平滑退化。
AI.relevance_reason: 其“描述子分辨率—下游收益”的量化关系可能为 LVR 中视觉证据需保留多少细节、视觉旁路的信息瓶颈度量提供参照，但原文属部署期分布偏移适配，与推理期 latent 状态生成和答案使用无直接联系。
